what_its_for: Nicotine polacrilex (gum or lozenge) helps you quit smoking or using other tobacco products. It gives your body a small, controlled amount of nicotine to reduce cravings and withdrawal symptoms like irritability, anxiety, and difficulty concentrating. This makes it easier to stop using tobacco without feeling so uncomfortable.
how_to_take: FOR GUM: Use the 'chew and park' method. Chew the gum slowly until you taste a tingling or peppery flavor, then 'park' it between your cheek and gum. When the tingling fades, chew it again, then park it again. Repeat this for about 30 minutes. Do NOT chew it like regular gum. FOR LOZENGE: Place it in your mouth and let it dissolve slowly over 20 to 30 minutes. Move it from side to side occasionally. Do NOT chew or swallow it whole. Do NOT eat or drink anything 15 minutes before or while using the gum or lozenge, as this can reduce how well it works.
dosing: Your dose depends on how soon you smoke your first cigarette after waking up. If you smoke within 30 minutes of waking up, use the HIGHER strength (4 mg gum or 4 mg lozenge). If you smoke 30 minutes or more after waking up, use the LOWER strength (2 mg gum or 2 mg lozenge). Typical schedule: Weeks 1 to 6 — use 1 piece every 1 to 2 hours. Weeks 7 to 9 — use 1 piece every 2 to 4 hours. Weeks 10 to 12 — use 1 piece every 4 to 8 hours. Use at least 9 pieces per day for the first 6 weeks. Do not use more than 24 pieces per day. The full treatment course is usually 12 weeks.
missed_dose: Nicotine polacrilex is used as needed to manage cravings rather than on a strict timed schedule. If you miss a scheduled piece and start feeling strong cravings, go ahead and use one. Do not double up by using two pieces at the same time to make up for a missed one. Try to stay as close to your planned schedule as possible to keep cravings under control.
storage: Store at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep away from heat and direct sunlight, as heat can soften the gum or lozenge. Keep out of reach of children and pets — even small amounts of nicotine can be very dangerous or fatal to children and animals. Dispose of used pieces carefully by wrapping them in paper and placing in the trash.
what_to_avoid: Do NOT smoke, use chewing tobacco, or use any other nicotine products (patches, inhalers, nasal sprays) while using this product unless directed by your doctor, as you could get too much nicotine. Avoid eating or drinking for 15 minutes before and during use, especially acidic foods and drinks like coffee, juice, or soda, as they can reduce effectiveness. Do not use more than the recommended amount. Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery if you feel dizzy or lightheaded after use.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor or seek medical attention if you experience: chest pain, irregular or fast heartbeat, severe dizziness or fainting, nausea or vomiting that is severe, jaw pain or mouth sores that do not go away, signs of too much nicotine such as severe headache, cold sweats, or weakness, difficulty breathing or swallowing, or if you have been using this product for more than 12 weeks and are still unable to quit. Also call your doctor before using this product if you are pregnant, recently had a heart attack, have severe heart disease, or have any mouth or throat problems.
when_it_works: Most people begin to notice reduced cravings and withdrawal symptoms within the first few days of use. The full benefit builds over the first few weeks as you follow the recommended schedule. Quitting tobacco is a process, and it may take several attempts. Using this product as directed for the full 12 weeks gives you the best chance of success. Some people notice that urges to smoke decrease significantly within the first 2 weeks.
special_populations: PREGNANCY: Talk to your doctor before using. Quitting smoking is very important during pregnancy, but your doctor can help decide the safest option for you and your baby. BREASTFEEDING: Nicotine passes into breast milk. Ask your doctor before using. TEENAGERS (under 18): Do not use without a doctor's guidance. HEART CONDITIONS: Talk to your doctor first if you have had a recent heart attack, have angina, or have an irregular heartbeat. DIABETES: Monitor blood sugar more closely, as quitting tobacco can affect blood sugar levels. DENTAL ISSUES: If you have dentures, braces, or dental work, the gum form may not be suitable — ask your doctor about the lozenge instead.
